regions.label: MZ header
regions.note: DOS EXE header, rebuilt by the museum unpacker after removing the DIET compression.

regions.label: Relocation table
regions.note: 4,225 addresses that DOS patches at load time, almost all of them far calls between code segments.

regions.label: Header padding
regions.note: Fills the header to a 16-byte boundary.

regions.label: Borland C++ startup (c0)
regions.note: Sets up memory and the stack, then calls main() at 0E9D:000F with far argv and envp.

regions.label: Borland C++ runtime library
regions.note: File I/O, memory, strings and conio.

regions.label: Truth-table printer
regions.note: Prints the truth table to PRN, one character at a time through DOS INT 21h function 05h.

regions.label: Analysis engine
regions.note: Truth table, fault dictionary and the recursive test-pattern search (the largest module, 20,704 bytes).

regions.label: Netlist builder and shared helpers
regions.note: Turns the drawing into gates; also holds compiler copies of class-library inline functions such as Object::Object().

regions.label: Logic element base class
regions.note: Five-valued AND, OR and NOT, and setting a pin value with a conflict check.

regions.label: main()
regions.note: Creates the four catalogs (gates, chips, technologies, circuits) and starts BGI graphics.

regions.label: Gate class
regions.note: Evaluates a gate in five-valued logic; saves and loads .GAT files.

regions.label: Drawing helpers
regions.note: Text placement and sizing for the screen.

regions.label: Chip definition class
regions.note: Pin maps of the 74xx chips; saves and loads .IC files.

regions.label: Sheet object base class
regions.note: Base class of everything drawn on the circuit sheet, and the chip symbol class.

regions.label: Wire class
regions.note: A wire between two pins, stored as keypad direction digits.

regions.label: Circuit propagation helpers
regions.note: Moves values through the circuit; two classes built on Borland Array and SortedArray.

regions.label: Node class
regions.note: A junction where several wires meet.

regions.label: Sheet helpers
regions.note: Three small methods used by the circuit sheet.

regions.label: Pin terminal class
regions.note: Circuit inputs, outputs, VCC and GND.

regions.label: Circuit sheet class
regions.note: The 30,105-byte circuit object with its cell grid; saves and loads .CIR files.

regions.label: Main window and menus
regions.note: Draws the frame and menus with 283 BGI calls and starts the graphics with auto-detect.

regions.label: SPARR.CPP: second root class and sparse array
regions.note: The root class of every sheet and file class, its own operator new, and a sparse array class built like Borland's ABSTARRY.CPP.

regions.label: Technology class
regions.note: Logic families TTL and TTL open-collector; saves and loads .TCK files.

regions.label: Group catalog class
regions.note: Names member files FILn, keeps the previous save as BFLn, and writes and checks the 4-byte size trailer.

regions.label: Borland container class library
regions.note: Object, AbstractArray, Array, SortedArray and Error (ABSTARRY.CPP), compiled into the program.

regions.label: Chip symbol drawing
regions.note: Draws each chip with its gate labels: a jump table on the part number, 7400 to 7440.

regions.label: File dialog
regions.note: Asks for a file name and lists catalog entries.

regions.label: Dialogs and windows
regions.note: Pop-up windows and their frames.

regions.label: IC tester and alarm
regions.note: The IC TESTER screen and a two-tone speaker alarm written in inline assembly.

regions.label: Probe prompts
regions.note: Tells the user where to apply the input and output probes, GND and VCC.

regions.label: Fault location and test-card I/O
regions.note: Applies test patterns through ports 301h and 300h, reads the answers, and runs the guided probe.

regions.label: Menu commands
regions.note: Runs the FILE, OBJECTS, ANALYZE and PRINT commands.

regions.label: Borland BGI graphics library
regions.note: initgraph, line, bar, outtextxy and the rest; loads EGAVGA.BGI and the .CHR fonts from disk.

regions.label: Far globals
regions.note: Far global variables, 16 bytes each (for example the current circuit pointer at 2ADF:0000).

regions.label: Runtime start-up data
regions.note: Borland copyright string and runtime error messages.

regions.label: Strings, file headers and vtables
regions.note: Truth-table text, catalog names, the KEMYAM copyright headers of every file type, and the vtables of his classes.

regions.label: Class-library data
regions.note: Messages and vtables of the Borland container classes (ABSTARRY.CPP, Array, SortedArray).

regions.label: Menus and prompts
regions.note: Menu text, the About box with five student names, help lines and probe prompts.

regions.label: Runtime data
regions.note: File handle table, file mode, stack size and C++ runtime messages.

regions.label: BGI data
regions.note: Font and driver names (TRIP, LITT, EGAVGA...) and graphics error messages.

regions.label: Zero-filled variables
regions.note: Variables that start as zero.

routines.name: main
routines.note: Builds the four catalogs, starts the BGI graphics, then runs the menu loop.

lines.note: Window setup, which starts the graphics with auto-detect

routines.name: Gate::Gate
routines.note: Constructor: allocates 28 bytes if needed, calls the base constructor, installs the Gate method table, loads the .GAT file.

lines.note: Install the Gate method table at DS:0335

routines.name: Gate::evaluate
routines.note: Counts the inputs by value (controlling, non-controlling, D, D-bar, unknown); D and D-bar together count as the controlling value.

lines.note: Compare an input with the controlling value
Unknown inputs plus a fault value: mark the gate as D-frontier

routines.name: Gate::load
routines.note: Reads a .GAT file and checks its KEMYAM header.

routines.name: Gate::save
routines.note: Writes header, Ctrl-Z, then 6 bytes at offset 32h.

lines.note: Ctrl-Z (1Ah) right after the copyright text
Seek to offset 32h: the data always starts there

routines.name: and5
routines.note: Five-valued AND: any 0 wins; D AND D-bar is 0; X spreads.

routines.name: or5
routines.note: Five-valued OR, the mirror of AND.

routines.name: not5
routines.note: NOT by jump table: 1 and 2 swap (0 and 1), 6 and 9 swap (D and D-bar), anything else becomes X (15).

routines.name: truth_table
routines.note: Tries all 2^n input rows with an odometer counter and prints each row.

lines.note: Input is 0? make it 1 and stop
Else make it 0 and carry to the next input

routines.name: make_dictionary
routines.note: The fault dictionary command: a fixed pipeline of passes over the circuit.

routines.name: search
routines.note: Recursive search that resets values to X (15) as it backs out (backtracking).

routines.name: dos_write
routines.note: Raw DOS write in inline assembly, used by the .CIR save.

routines.name: Group::create
routines.note: Before saving FILn, deletes BFLn and renames FILn to BFLn, then opens the file for writing.

routines.name: Group::read
routines.note: Opens a member file, compares its last 4 bytes with its length, then reads it whole.

lines.note: Trailer equals the file length? Otherwise the file is refused

routines.name: Group::close
routines.note: Appends the 4-byte size trailer and closes the file.

routines.name: Circuit::save
routines.note: Writes all parts first, then all wires with their keypad paths.

routines.name: card_apply
routines.note: Reverses the 8 test bits, writes them to port 301h and one bit to port 300h, then reads port 300h 2,000 times.

lines.note: IN 300h, 2,000 times; the last reading is kept
Store the answer in place of the pattern

routines.name: probe_read
routines.note: Guided probe: reads port 300h 2,001 times and keeps bit 3 of the last read, as code 1 (0) or 2 (1).

routines.name: alarm
routines.note: Two-tone speaker alarm: 20 tones, 1,193 Hz and 746 Hz in turn.

routines.name: lprint
routines.note: Sends a string to the printer with DOS function 05h, in inline assembly.

routines.name: write (Borland)
routines.note: Runtime write(): in text mode it writes 0Dh before every 0Ah, the DOS line ending.
